Experimental. A Juniper Junos device's host name. Removing this step leaves the name as it is.

**Experimental.** Network devices are new, and this module may change between releases. It's tested against vJunos-switch 26.2R1.7 on a lab VM, not yet in CI.

Use `junos_hostname` to name a Juniper Junos device. The change goes in like every Junos step does: a dry run first, then `commit confirmed`, then a confirm over a new login, once per device per circuit. See [`junos_config`](/modules/junos_config).

## Example usage

```hcl
step "name" {
  junos_hostname {
    name = each.key
  }
}
```

## Arguments

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | Yes | Host name, such as sw1. Junos takes letters, digits, hyphens and dots. |

## Read-only attributes

Conn3x sets these; reference them as `conn3x_junos_hostname.<circuit>__<step>["<host>"].<name>`.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `in_sync` | bool | Whether the device had this name at the last refresh. |
| `revision` | string | Changes each time Conn3x changes this on the host. Handlers watch it. |

A step lowers to the `conn3x_junos_hostname` resource, one instance per host, and connects with its circuit's `ssh` block.
